exact_excerpt: We next determined whether any of the genes are expressed in the pharyngeal apparatus or heart in embryos. Probes were generated, and in situ hybridization was successfully performed for *Gpr98, Cetn3*, *Lysmd3*, and *Mef2c* in mouse embryos at E9.5 and E10.5, when the cardiac OFT is expanding (Figure [3](#F3)). Although *Gpr98* is weakly expressed at E9.5, it is strongly expressed in the neural tube region, particularly the hindbrain [^29] (Figure [3](#F3)). *Cetn3*, important in the cilia [^30] for centrosome reproduction,[^31] and *Lysmd3*, of unknown function, are ubiquitously expressed, although *Cetn3* has lower expression levels in the heart itself (Figure [3](#F3)). *Mef2c* encodes a MADS box transcription factor, and it is expressed in the pharyngeal apparatus including the second heart field mesoderm,[^32] as indicated in Figure [3](#F3). Among the genes in the TAD, *MEF2C* is the only one specifically expressed in cardiac progenitor cells known to be required for heart development.[^33]

The gene biomarkers were tested using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test on the [GSE113439](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE113439) dataset, as shown in [Fig 9](#pone.0314319.g009). Seven genes (PTGS2, TBXA2R, GPR171, KLC3, MSRA, LYSMD3, and CMTM5) showed significant differences between the disease and control groups.
